title: Carry the inferred column axis into clip's where operation
answers: Why does DataFrame.clip require an axis for an extension-dtype bound?
Which axis does clipping use when an array or Index bound is supplied without axis?
How should clip pass an aligned Series bound to where?
body:
Symptom: DataFrame.clip with an extension-dtype array or Index bound and no axis raises ValueError: Must specify axis=0 or 1.
Root cause: pandas/core/generic.py:NDFrame._clip_with_one_bound passed axis=None onward after _align_for_op had converted the bound to a Series aligned against the columns; subsequent DataFrame-Series alignment requires an explicit axis.
Fix pattern: Carry the inferred alignment axis forward: when operand alignment returns a Series and axis is None, set axis=1 before calling where.
Constraints: Apply this inference in the non-Series list-like bound conversion path; preserve explicit axis=0 and axis=1. pandas/tests/frame/methods/test_clip.py:TestDataFrameClip.test_clip_extension_dtype_bound checks column-default behavior and equivalent inplace and returned results.
applies: DataFrame.clip's conversion of non-Series list-like bounds when the caller omits axis.
